subject: Using c-hat value to adjust predicted occupancy from the 'predict()' function

messages.author: 9c5d22292e637ac4
messages.subject: Using c-hat value to adjust predicted occupancy from the 'predict()' function
parts:
Hi all,

I am using a single top-ranked model from my candidate set of models, to predict occupancy using the standard technique of creating a new data frame and going for the following approach:
predict(top-ranked model, type = "state", newdata = newdata, appendData = TRUE)

The issue is that there is some overdispersion in my global model, such that I would like to use that overdispersion factor (c-hat value of 1.31) to adjust the standard errors of my top-ranked model and use that in the predicted occupancy. 

I know that I can get the corrected parameter estimates using 'summaryOD()'. But I would like to know how I can get the overdispersion-corrected predicted values using the above 'predict()' function or any other function? The end output would be to show these predicted values against the site and observation covariates as a graph.

My apologies if this has been covered elsewhere, but I was not able to find the right resources for this.

Thank you in advance for any insights!
Ramya

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Using c-hat value to adjust predicted occupancy from the 'predict()' function
parts:
Dear Ramya,

when we published the AHM1 book in 2016, we had the following (Section 6.9.4):

"Function modavgPred in AICcmodavg can be tricked into producing point predictions with SEs
and 95% CIs by providing a candidate list with a single model only. As of August 2015, no
CIs are available, though for some cases 95% CIs can be obtained by adding/subtracting
twice the SEs from the point estimates on the link scale and then applying the inverse link
transformation.

# Predictions for lambda and p, incl. SE and with overdispersion, but no CIs
# Poisson model, for natural and for link scale of both lambda and p
modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type
= "response", c.hat = 3.82)
modavgPred(cand.set = list(fm5), newdata=lamNewData, parm.type = "lambda", type
= "link", c.hat = 3.82) # Could be used to get 95% CIs"

Surely something like this still works.

Best regards  ---- Marc
